claims.value: Bodart: side A (French) 30,000 infantry and 5,000 cavalry, total 35,000; side B (Spanish) 41,000 infantry and 4,000 cavalry, total 45,000.
claims.rationale: Available-for-engagement figures under Bodart’s rounded-up convention (shared research-conventions index), unless the entry specifies a surrender population. claims.value: Toreno gives side B scarcely 41,000 if joined with Aragon, including 3,700 cavalry, but 20,000 in the fifth division and Aragonese near Tudela.
claims.rationale: Combined army, geographical spread and local concentration remain distinct, not additive. English rendering (ours): "His forces, if joined with Aragon, scarcely reached 41,000 including 3,700 cavalry; both [the fifth division and Aragonese] together numbered 20,000."

claims.value: Napoleon reported sending Lannes to command Moncey’s corps and Lagrange’s division, march on Tudela and attack.
claims.rationale: English rendering (ours): "Marshal Lannes has left to take command of Moncey’s corps and Lagrange’s division, march straight on Tudela and attack the enemy."

claims.value: Toreno says Aragonese troops refused to join without Palafox’s express order; O’Neil commanded them near Tudela and Castaños gave field orders.
claims.rationale: Contingent authority and field orders do not establish a single unbroken chief-command relationship. English rendering (ours): "They refused to join without General Palafox’s express order; Don Juan O’Neil had camped with the Aragonese across Tudela since the previous day; O’Neil acted on Castaños’s order."

claims.value: Napoleon later claimed only 6,000 French had scarcely been able to engage against 30,000 enemy troops.
claims.rationale: Retrospective interested claim about engaged subset; not a full French return or resolution of the Spanish army total. English rendering (ours): "There were 30,000 elite troops and 60 guns at Tudela; scarcely 6,000 of ours could engage."

citations.quote: Il y avait cependant à Tudela 30,000 hommes de troupes d’élite, 60 pièces de canon : 6,000 hommes des nôtres ont à peine pu donner.

claims.value: The French offensive against Tudela was ordered by Napoleon through Lannes.
claims.rationale: English rendering (ours): "march straight on Tudela and attack the enemy."

claims.value: Toreno says the whole Spanish army extended over four leagues between Tarazona and Tudela.
claims.rationale: English rendering (ours): "The whole army was spread over the four leagues between the last city [Tarazona] and Tudela."

open_questions: Separate Tudela, Cascante and unengaged Tarazona forces; establish the effective Castaños/Palafox/O’Neil authority and French engaged subset.
Deferred: the dated original returns and reports identified above, and any deeper source-lineage reconciliation. No additional research cycle follows merely from this gap.

Source dependence: Bodart is a later compilation. Toreno, Foy, Oman, Saint-Cyr and the official Correspondance are interested or retrospective source families, and embedded/reprinted reports are not extra independent witnesses. Agreement does not establish independence.

A.strength_population_and_time: Bodart’s engagement-level available force; no dated opening return. Source-specific alternatives below retain their own moment and population. Alternatives/limits: Napoleon later claimed only 6,000 French had scarcely been able to engage against 30,000 enemy troops.
A.command_scope: Printed side-A commander Lannes; local/superior authority and transitions remain limited to the additional passages cited below. Napoleon reported sending Lannes to command Moncey’s corps and Lagrange’s division, march on Tudela and attack.
A.army_continuity: Unknown: these passages do not establish a cross-engagement army identity.

B.strength_population_and_time: Bodart’s engagement-level available force; no dated opening return. Civilians, recruits, regular troops and surrender survivors are not interchangeable. Alternatives/limits: Toreno gives side B scarcely 41,000 if joined with Aragon, including 3,700 cavalry, but 20,000 in the fifth division and Aragonese near Tudela.
B.command_scope: Printed side-B commander Castaños; local/superior authority and transitions remain limited to the additional passages cited below. Toreno says Aragonese troops refused to join without Palafox’s express order; O’Neil commanded them near Tudela and Castaños gave field orders.
